properties.areaDesc: Spartanburg, SC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 10:50PM EDT until October 11 at 4:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Spartanburg County in upstate South Carolina...

* Until 430 AM EDT.

* At 1050 PM EDT, Earlier today, a prolonged period of steady
rainfall produced 2.5-4 inches across Spartanburg County,
saturating area soils and causing isolated areas of nuisance
flooding.  Doppler radar shows an axis of torrential rainfall has
moved into Spartanburg County from the south, capable of producing
1-2 inches of rainfall on top of saturated soils.  This rainfall
will exacerbate areas of ongoing nuisance flooding and cause new
areas of flooding to develop. The heaviest rainfall is currently
impacting Cross Anchor, Enoree, and Pauiine.

* Areas of greatest concern include along Lawsons Fork Creek and
Meadow Creek near Inman; the South Pacolet River, Motlow Creek, and
Holston Creek near Campobello; Bear Creek and Obed Creek north of
Lake Bowen; and areas near Croft State Park.  Earlier, Glendale
Fire Department reported nuisance flooding along Country Club Rd
near Church St.  Flood conditions there are likely to worsen.
Please obey all barricades and avoid flooded roadways.  Only a few
inches of water can strand your vehicle.

* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the
next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-
access areas, and  campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Spartanburg, Boiling Springs SC, Woodruff, Lyman, Pacolet, Cowpens,
Wellford, Inman, Mayo and Roebuck.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 10:47PM EDT until October 11 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...In Northeast Georgia, the following counties: Elbert,
Franklin, Habersham, Hart, Rabun and Stephens. In western North
Carolina, the following counties: Avery, Buncombe, Burke, Caldwell,
McDowell, Polk,  Rutherford, Haywood, Henderson, Macon, Mitchell,
Jackson, Transylvania and Yancey. In Upstate South Carolina, the
following counties: Abbeville, Anderson, Central Greenville,
Greater Oconee, Greater Pickens, Greenville, Greenwood, Laurens,
Spartanburg, and Oconee.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- As the remnants of Isaias move northward into the lower Ohio
Valley, periods of rain will continue. High rainfall rates will
continue in short bursts through the overnight hours. By Sunday
morning, total accumulations of generally 5 to 8 inches are
expected along the southeast-facing Blue Ridge Escarpment, with 2
to 5 inches elsewhere in the watch area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Watch for flash flooding means there is a potential for rapid
onset flooding based on current forecasts. Flash flooding is a very
dangerous situation and may impact areas that do not typically flood.
Please monitor the latest forecasts and be prepared to take action
quickly should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Rainfall of more than five inches in similar storms has been
associated with an increased risk of landslides, especially
fast-moving debris flows and debris slides. If you live on a
mountainside or in a cove at the base of a mountain, especially near
a stream, be ready to leave in advance of the storm and follow
evacuation orders from local officials. Consider postponing travel
along mountain roads during the heavy rainfall event.

properties.areaDesc: Lancaster; Middlesex; Mathews
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 10:42PM EDT until October 11 at 4:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Lancaster, Middlesex and Mathews Counties.

* WHEN...From 9 AM to 4 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Shallow flooding is expected in the most vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Expect up to one foot of water
above ground level in low lying, vulnerable areas. Some roads
and low lying property including parking lots, parks and lawns
near the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
